name: Osama bin Laden
summary: Bin Laden advocated an Islamic political order governed by scripture and armed jihad against governments and foreign powers he treated as enemies of Islam. He directed and justified terrorist attacks on civilians, rejected Israel’s legitimacy and promoted antisemitic conspiracy claims. His statements also opposed interest-based finance, corporate political power and environmental destruction.

sources.title: Compilation of Usama Bin Ladin Statements, 1994–January 2004
sources.author: Osama bin Laden; FBIS translations
sources.usedFor: Full 289-page compilation downloaded and searched; 1996 declaration pp.13–27, 1997 interview pp.46–47, 1998 declaration pp.56–58, 2002 letter pp.214–220 and January 2004 address pp.275–278. Only first-person statements are evidence of views.

sources.title: Full Transcript of Bin Laden Video (29 October 2004)
sources.author: Osama bin Laden; government translation reproduced by ABC News
sources.usedFor: Acknowledgment of directing the September 11 attack and stated motives; full text downloaded.

sources.title: To the American people (undated recovered letter, after Obama took office)
sources.author: Attributed to Osama bin Laden; ODNI declassified translation
sources.usedFor: Full recovered letter downloaded; corporate influence, bank bailouts, climate and rejection of a two-state solution. Unsigned attribution is noted and confidence limited.

sources.title: The 9/11 Commission Report, chapter 2
sources.author: National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States
sources.usedFor: Investigated record of his organisation and attacks, checked against his own statements.

sources.title: Interview with Hamid Mir (November 2001)
sources.author: Osama bin Laden / Dawn
sources.usedFor: Claimed nuclear deterrence only; not proof that he possessed weapons.

sources.title: Reevaluating Al-Qa`ida’s Weapons of Mass Destruction Capabilities (2010)
sources.author: Peter Bergen / Combating Terrorism Center at West Point
sources.usedFor: Reported personal meetings about nuclear capability and distinction between his weapons claims and evidence.
